title: Rate of steady-state heat conduction through two-layer composite slab

question.statement: The temperature of the two outer surfaces of a composite slab, consisting of two materials having coefficients of thermal conductivity $K$ and $2K$ and thickness $x$ and $4x$, respectively, are $T_2$ and $T_1$ ($T_2 > T_1$). The rate of heat transfer through the slab, in a steady state is $\left(\frac{A(T_2 - T_1)K}{x}\right)f$. Find the value of $F$.

figure_refs.caption: Composite slab consisting of two materials in thermal contact: the first slab of thickness $x$ with thermal conductivity $K$, and the second slab of thickness $4x$ with thermal conductivity $2K$, with outer boundary temperatures $T_2$ and $T_1$.
figure_refs.alt_text: Schematic diagram of two conducting slabs placed in series. The left slab has thickness x and thermal conductivity K, with left boundary at temperature T2. The right slab has thickness 4x and thermal conductivity 2K, with right boundary at temperature T1.
